text: The next shift is waiting.
Maya has two minutes to get a maintenance update ready.
An agent can do it in seconds.
She asks for an update. Not a publication.
But a helpful next step can cross a line she never meant to cross.
The note moves toward a shared repository.
An internal-only detail goes with it.
The draft took seconds. The damage lasts longer.
Rewind. A prompt is not a policy.
The organization owns the rules. Not the model.
Same request. This time, through Airlock.
The local work goes through. A real draft lands in the local outbox.
Nothing goes online.
Then comes a proposed push. The first gate says no.
No online writes. Its code matches the push against a separate rule file.
The hook denies it before execution.
A second gate checks the draft itself.
Sensitive information. An internal-only label means ask first.
Here, approval isn't implemented. So it stays blocked.
The runtime records the rule, the verdict, and the time.
Not a promise. A record someone can inspect.
Local evidence. Not tamper-proof.
A local prototype. Not a sandbox for every process.
The organization sets what agents may do.
Airlock makes that binding on the paths it checks.
